config.theme: Incident postmortem: the checkout outage last Tuesday
config.author: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Code session)

cast.theme: Incident postmortem: the checkout outage last Tuesday

personas.name: Imani
personas.goals: A clear record and fixes that stick
personas.hidden_agenda: Pushed for load testing last year and lost the budget fight

personas.name: Gareth
personas.role: Backend engineer who made the rate limit change
personas.hidden_agenda: Was asked to make the change by the security team in a hurry

personas.name: Selin
personas.goals: Look after the customers who were hurt
personas.hidden_agenda: Her call center staff were abused on the phones all morning

personas.name: Pablo
personas.hidden_agenda: The portal redesign launch is in two weeks and he's worried it slips

agenda.title: Cause
agenda.goal: Understand the rate limit change and the due-date spike

facts.statement: New rate limit = 500 requests per second
Average hold time at peak = 38 minutes
Customers with bills due that day = 120,000
The rate limit change was CHG-2207
Previous peak handled = 1,100 requests per second
Status page updated 25 minutes after the start

beats.summary: The rate limit change; Gareth misstates the new limit and is corrected
The human side; Selin's hold time is high, corrected later; Pablo's failure count stands
Owners, dates, and one open question

turns.speaker: Imani
turns.text: Thanks for coming. Blameless, as usual. Let's start with the timeline.

turns.speaker: Gareth
turns.text: The portal started rejecting payments at five past eight in the morning.

turns.speaker: Pablo
turns.text: Which is exactly when people pay their bills before work.

turns.speaker: Imani
turns.text: When did the status page go up?

turns.speaker: Selin
turns.text: Twenty-five minutes later. My team was already drowning by then.

turns.speaker: Imani
turns.text: How long was the portal down in total?

turns.speaker: Gareth
turns.text: Ninety-five minutes, until the limit was raised again.

turns.speaker: Selin
turns.text: It felt like a whole day on the phones.

turns.speaker: Pablo
turns.text: I was on the train when it started. My own payment failed. That's how I found out.

turns.speaker: Imani
turns.text: Not ideal, but at least you saw what customers saw.

turns.speaker: Pablo
turns.text: I saw a page that said "too many requests". Customers have no idea what that means.

turns.speaker: Selin
turns.text: They thought we were blaming them for paying too often.

turns.speaker: Imani
turns.text: That error message is going on the action list.

turns.speaker: Gareth
turns.text: In fairness, it's the default message from the gateway. Nobody ever wrote a friendly one.

turns.speaker: Selin
turns.text: Then let's write one.

turns.speaker: Imani
turns.text: Gareth, what changed?

turns.speaker: Gareth
turns.text: The security team asked us to add a rate limit on the payment API after the credential-stuffing attempts last month. I set it to a thousand requests a second.

turns.speaker: Imani
turns.text: The change ticket says five hundred. CHG-2207.

turns.speaker: Gareth
turns.text: Five hundred. You're right. A thousand was the number I'd proposed, and it got lowered in review.

turns.speaker: Pablo
turns.text: And the traffic that morning?

turns.speaker: Gareth
turns.text: It peaked at fourteen hundred a second. Almost three times the limit.

turns.speaker: Selin
turns.text: Why that morning in particular?

turns.speaker: Pablo
turns.text: A hundred and twenty thousand customers had bills due that day. It's the first of the month.

turns.speaker: Imani
turns.text: Had we ever seen that much traffic before?

turns.speaker: Gareth
turns.text: The previous peak was eleven hundred. So even the old high-water mark would have been blocked.

turns.speaker: Imani
turns.text: So the limit was set without anyone checking real traffic.

turns.speaker: Gareth
turns.text: Without anyone checking the first of the month, no. The security team looked at an average day.

turns.speaker: Selin
turns.text: An average day is not the day people pay their bills.

turns.speaker: Imani
turns.text: It's a gap in how we review limits, not in Gareth.

turns.speaker: Pablo
turns.text: Has the security team been told what happened?

turns.speaker: Imani
turns.text: I spoke to their lead yesterday. They're joining the actions part next week.

turns.speaker: Gareth
turns.text: Rate limits should be set from the busiest day of the year, not an average. That should be a rule.

turns.speaker: Imani
turns.text: Then that's the rule from today: limits are set from the busiest day in the last year, with headroom.

turns.speaker: Selin
turns.text: Good.

turns.speaker: Gareth
turns.text: I'll rewrite the limit using the first-of-month peaks and get it reviewed by both teams.

turns.speaker: Imani
turns.text: Customers. Selin?

turns.speaker: Selin
turns.text: We took forty-two hundred calls that morning. Hold times hit an hour at the worst point.

turns.speaker: Pablo
turns.text: And about five thousand payments failed outright.

turns.speaker: Imani
turns.text: Those people will get late fees, unless we waive them.

turns.speaker: Selin
turns.text: We have to waive them. It wasn't their fault.

turns.speaker: Pablo
turns.text: Waiving every late fee from that morning is seventy-three and a half thousand dollars. Finance already ran it.

turns.speaker: Imani
turns.text: That's a lot, but it's the right thing.

turns.speaker: Selin
turns.text: Some customers were in tears on the phone. One woman thought her heating would be cut off.

turns.speaker: Pablo
turns.text: Was it?

turns.speaker: Selin
turns.text: No. Nobody gets disconnected for a missed payment on a day we were down. We made sure of that.

turns.speaker: Imani
turns.text: Then we waive every late fee caused by the outage, automatically, with no need to call.

turns.speaker: Selin
turns.text: Could someone send customers an apology that explains it in plain words?

turns.speaker: Pablo
turns.text: I'll write it today, and get Selin to read it before it goes.

turns.speaker: Selin
turns.text: Thank you. Sorry, one more correction. I checked the call log after the meeting started. The average hold at peak was thirty-eight minutes, not an hour.

turns.speaker: Imani
turns.text: Thirty-eight minutes is still terrible.

turns.speaker: Selin
turns.text: It is. My team deserves a thank-you, honestly.

turns.speaker: Pablo
turns.text: The weather didn't help, either. That freezing fog had half the city working from home and online at eight.

turns.speaker: Gareth
turns.text: The fog was wild. I couldn't see the end of my street.

turns.speaker: Selin
turns.text: My kids had a snow day and there wasn't even any snow.

turns.speaker: Pablo
turns.text: Actions, then.

turns.speaker: Imani
turns.text: Actions. We have Gareth on the limit, Pablo on the apology, and the fees waived automatically.

turns.speaker: Selin
turns.text: And the error message. Customers need to know it's us, not them.

turns.speaker: Pablo
turns.text: That one's mine. The new message will say we're having trouble and their payment hasn't been taken.

turns.speaker: Gareth
turns.text: It might be worth load-testing the portal before the redesign launch too.

turns.speaker: Imani
turns.text: I'd like that very much. I'll put a load test in the launch checklist.

turns.speaker: Pablo
turns.text: Will the load test delay the redesign? It launches in two weeks.

turns.speaker: Imani
turns.text: Not if we start it this week. A day of testing, maybe two.

turns.speaker: Selin
turns.text: Who checks that the late-fee waivers actually went through for everyone?

turns.speaker: Gareth
turns.text: I can pull a report of every failed payment from that morning, if that helps whoever does it.

turns.speaker: Imani
turns.text: Thank you, everyone. This was a hard morning for a lot of people, and you handled it well.
